text:
If you've got outdoor plans today, keep them flexible and keep an eye to the sky, because the showers and storms just keep coming in waves. Morning rain should taper by 11, but by early afternoon another round of showers and thunderstorms moves in, with a high near 85 and that thick, soupy humidity sticking around all day. NWS has this at a 70% chance, and the wetter models agree, so don't be surprised if you get caught out there. On the lake, southeast winds under 10 knots today, waves a foot or less, but with storms in the mix I'd be off the broad waters well before the afternoon round arrives. Tonight's better, drier, just a 40% shot of a stray shower.

Sunday's the payoff: that cold front finally clears us out, morning showers wrap up early, then mostly sunny skies, a high near 86, and noticeably lower humidity by afternoon. West wind picks up a touch, seas 1 to 2 feet on the lake, but a much nicer day to be out on the water or the trails. Good call for today: get your outdoor time in before early afternoon, then let the storms pass and save the longer plans for tomorrow.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Scattered showers and thunderstorms will continue today, but they will be more widely scattered compared to last night. Severe weather isn’t expected, but there could be locally an inch or more of rain in any thunderstorms with isolated flash flooding not out of the question. A cold front will come through tonight and into Sunday, leaving us with just the chance for a few showers or thunderstorms in the Northeast Kingdom on Sunday. The humidity will be kicked down a notch Sunday afternoon. High temperatures over the weekend will be in the 80s.
